name: National Environmental Policy Act
description: Requires environmental impact statements for major federal actions. Forms basis for pipeline permitting environmental review.
market_impact: Creates multi-year permitting timeline for major pipelines. Extended review process can delay infrastructure by 3-10 years.
quantitative_impact: Average pipeline EIS takes 4-6 years to complete

name: FERC Order 436
description: First major step toward open-access gas transportation. Allowed pipelines to offer transportation services on a non-discriminatory basis, beginning unbundling of merchant and transportation functions.
market_impact: Began transition from regulated wellhead prices to market-based pricing. Created framework for third-party access to pipelines.

name: Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990
description: Established SO2 cap-and-trade program for power plants. First major market-based emissions trading program.
market_impact: Required scrubbers or fuel switching for high-sulfur coal plants. Began shift toward low-sulfur western coal and natural gas.
quantitative_impact: SO2 emissions from power sector fell 90% since 1990

name: FERC Order 636
description: Landmark restructuring order that required interstate pipelines to unbundle their sales services from transportation services. Created the modern competitive natural gas market structure.
market_impact: Completed transition to competitive wholesale gas markets. Enabled gas marketing companies, spot markets, and financial derivatives. Henry Hub emerged as primary pricing point.
quantitative_impact: Wellhead prices declined ~30% in real terms 1992-1998

name: FERC Order 888
description: Required all public utilities owning transmission to provide open-access transmission services. Foundation for wholesale electricity competition and ISO/RTO formation.
market_impact: Enabled wholesale electricity markets, ISOs, and competitive power generation. Gas-fired generation became economically viable for merchant plants.
quantitative_impact: Led to formation of ISOs covering >60% of US load

name: FERC Certificate Policy Statement
description: Established framework for evaluating natural gas pipeline certificate applications. Balanced economic need against environmental and landowner impacts.
market_impact: Provided predictable framework for pipeline approvals. Currently under review for potential updates regarding climate impacts.
quantitative_impact: FERC approved ~95% of pipeline applications 2000-2020

name: FERC Order 2000
description: Encouraged formation of Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs) to operate transmission grids and administer wholesale markets.
market_impact: Created organized wholesale markets (PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE). Enabled transparent price signals and efficient dispatch.
quantitative_impact: RTOs now serve ~2/3 of US electricity demand

name: Energy Policy Act 2005 - Hydraulic Fracturing Exemption
description: Exempted hydraulic fracturing from Safe Drinking Water Act regulation. Removed regulatory barriers to shale gas development.
market_impact: Enabled rapid scale-up of shale gas production. US gas production increased from 18 Tcf (2005) to 34 Tcf (2023). Transformed US from net importer to net exporter.
quantitative_impact: Henry Hub fell from $8-13/MMBtu (2005-2008) to $2-4/MMBtu (2012-2020)

name: Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative
description: First mandatory cap-and-trade program for CO2 in US. Currently covers 11 Northeast and Mid-Atlantic states.
market_impact: Carbon price adds $2-15/MWh to coal and gas generation costs. Accelerated coal retirements in region. Raised >$6B in allowance revenue.
quantitative_impact: Carbon price ~$13/ton (2024); regional emissions down 50% since 2005

name: DOE LNG Export Authorization - FTA Countries
description: LNG exports to Free Trade Agreement countries deemed in public interest and approved without additional review.
market_impact: Enabled initial LNG export project approvals. FTA countries include most of Americas, Australia, Korea.
quantitative_impact: Enabled ~25 Bcf/d of approved FTA export capacity

name: Sabine Pass LNG Export Authorization
description: First authorization to export LNG to non-FTA countries. Landmark decision enabling US LNG exports to Europe and Asia.
market_impact: Opened global markets for US LNG. Sabine Pass began exports Feb 2016, transforming US gas market dynamics.
quantitative_impact: US LNG exports: 0 (2015) to 12+ Bcf/d (2024)

name: California Global Warming Solutions Act
description: Established California cap-and-trade program and 2020 emission reduction targets. Extended by SB 32 with 2030 targets.
market_impact: Carbon price adds $15-30/MWh to fossil generation costs. Eliminated in-state coal. Linked with Quebec market.
quantitative_impact: Carbon price ~$30/ton (2024); no remaining coal generation in CA

name: Pennsylvania Act 13
description: Comprehensive regulation of Marcellus Shale drilling. Established impact fees, setback requirements, and preempted local zoning. Parts struck down by PA Supreme Court.
market_impact: Created regulatory framework for largest US shale gas play. Impact fees generated >$2B for local governments.
quantitative_impact: PA gas production: 1 Tcf (2010) to 7 Tcf (2023)

name: Cross-State Air Pollution Rule
description: Addresses interstate transport of NOx and SO2 emissions. Requires upwind states to reduce emissions contributing to downwind states ozone and PM2.5 nonattainment.
market_impact: Additional driver for coal plant emission controls or retirement. Updated multiple times with tighter limits.
quantitative_impact: Covers 27 states; contributed to coal retirements

name: Mercury and Air Toxics Standards
description: First national standards for mercury and other toxic air pollutants from power plants. Required emission controls or retirement.
market_impact: Major driver of coal plant retirements. Uneconomic to retrofit many older coal plants. Gas combined cycle became preferred replacement.
quantitative_impact: ~80 GW of coal retired 2010-2020, partially attributable to MATS

name: New York Fracking Ban
description: Permanent ban on high-volume hydraulic fracturing in New York State, citing health and environmental concerns.
market_impact: Prevented development of NY portion of Marcellus Shale. Increased NY dependence on pipeline imports from PA. Contributed to regional price basis differentials.
quantitative_impact: Algonquin Citygate basis vs Henry Hub widened during winter months

name: Colorado SB 19-181
description: Reformed Colorado oil and gas regulation to prioritize public health and environmental protection. Changed mission from "fostering" to "regulating" development. Allowed local government control.
market_impact: Increased regulatory uncertainty and compliance costs in DJ Basin. Some operators shifted capital to Permian.
quantitative_impact: DJ Basin rig count declined post-2019

name: Colorado Clean Energy Plan
description: Required Xcel Energy to reduce carbon 80% by 2030 and achieve 100% clean electricity by 2050. Accelerated coal plant retirements.
market_impact: Xcel retiring all CO coal by 2030. Massive renewable and storage buildout. Sets template for utility decarbonization plans.
quantitative_impact: ~3 GW coal to retire by 2030

name: Affordable Clean Energy Rule
description: Trump-era replacement for Clean Power Plan. Focused on heat rate improvements at individual plants rather than system-wide emission reductions.
market_impact: Vacated by DC Circuit in 2021. Regulatory uncertainty continued.
quantitative_impact: Vacated by court; no implementation

name: Texas SB 3 - Grid Reliability
description: Post-Winter Storm Uri reforms requiring weatherization of generation and gas facilities. Created Texas Energy Reliability Council.
market_impact: Increased compliance costs for generators. May reduce future extreme price events. Weatherization requirements phase in through 2023.
quantitative_impact: Weatherization costs estimated at $2-4B across ERCOT

name: Illinois Climate and Equitable Jobs Act
description: Mandates all coal plants close by 2030, all gas plants by 2045. 100% clean energy by 2050. Largest state-mandated coal phaseout.
market_impact: Will retire ~6 GW of coal in major MISO hub. Creates reliability planning challenges. Increases regional gas and renewable demand.
quantitative_impact: ~6 GW coal to retire by 2030

name: Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
description: $1.2T infrastructure bill including $65B for grid modernization, $8B for clean hydrogen hubs, $12B for carbon capture.
market_impact: Funding for transmission buildout, hydrogen hubs, and CCS demonstrations. Addresses key infrastructure bottlenecks.
quantitative_impact: $65B grid, $8B H2 hubs, $12B CCS

name: FERC GHG Policy Statements
description: Attempted to update pipeline certificate review to consider greenhouse gas emissions. Withdrawn after industry and political pushback.
market_impact: Created regulatory uncertainty. Subsequent pipeline applications faced increased scrutiny on climate impacts despite withdrawal.
quantitative_impact: Mountain Valley Pipeline delayed additional 2+ years partly due to climate litigation

name: Inflation Reduction Act
description: Largest climate investment in US history. Extended and expanded tax credits for wind, solar, storage, clean hydrogen, CCS, nuclear, and EVs.
market_impact: Major driver of renewable deployment and clean hydrogen economics. 10-year visibility on incentives enables project financing.
quantitative_impact: $369B in clean energy incentives; PTC/ITC extended through 2032+

name: Clean Hydrogen Production Tax Credit
description: Production tax credit up to $3/kg for clean hydrogen based on lifecycle carbon intensity. Four tiers from $0.60 to $3.00/kg.
market_impact: Transforms clean hydrogen economics. $3/kg credit makes green hydrogen competitive with grey in many applications.
quantitative_impact: Up to $3/kg credit for <0.45 kg CO2/kg H2

name: Mountain Valley Pipeline Approval
description: Fiscal Responsibility Act included provision directing completion of Mountain Valley Pipeline, overriding court challenges. First time Congress directly approved a specific pipeline.
market_impact: Enabled completion of 303-mile, 2 Bcf/d pipeline from Appalachia to Southeast. Set precedent for Congressional permitting intervention.
quantitative_impact: 2 Bcf/d capacity, in service Q1 2024

name: Good Neighbor Plan
description: Strengthened CSAPR to address 2015 ozone NAAQS transport. Requires significant NOx reductions from power plants and industrial sources in 23 states.
market_impact: Supreme Court stayed for some states. Where effective, accelerates need for emission controls or fuel switching.
quantitative_impact: Affects 23 states; Supreme Court partial stay complicates implementation

name: Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs Program
description: $7B to establish 7 regional clean hydrogen hubs across US. Covers production, storage, transport, and end-use infrastructure.
market_impact: Creates regional hydrogen ecosystems. Selected hubs span electrolytic, blue, and pink hydrogen pathways.
quantitative_impact: 7 hubs, $7B federal investment, expected to produce 3M metric tons H2/year

name: Methane Emissions Charge
description: IRA established first federal fee on methane emissions from petroleum and gas facilities. Starts at $900/ton in 2024, rises to $1,500/ton by 2026.
market_impact: Creates direct cost for methane emissions above threshold. Incentivizes leak detection and repair investments.

name: DOE LNG Export Permit Pause
description: Biden administration paused new LNG export authorizations to non-FTA countries pending updated economic and environmental analysis.
market_impact: Created uncertainty for ~10 Bcf/d of proposed projects. Did not affect projects already under construction or with existing authorizations.
quantitative_impact: Affects ~10 Bcf/d of proposed capacity, ~14 Bcf/d already approved continues

name: EPA Oil and Gas Methane Rule
description: First comprehensive federal regulation of methane from oil and gas operations. Requires leak detection, limits flaring, phases out routine venting.
market_impact: Increases compliance costs for producers. May accelerate consolidation to operators with better environmental performance.
quantitative_impact: Expected to reduce 58M metric tons CO2e by 2038

name: EPA Clean Power Plan 2.0 / Section 111 Rule
description: New GHG standards for power plants. Requires existing coal plants to reduce emissions 90% by 2032 or retire. New gas plants must use CCS by 2035.
market_impact: If upheld, will accelerate coal retirements and require carbon capture for new baseload gas. May affect 200+ GW of existing generation.
quantitative_impact: Could affect 200+ GW of existing fossil generation

name: ERCOT Performance Credit Mechanism
description: New reliability mechanism awarding credits to generators for availability during scarcity conditions. Alternative to traditional capacity market.
market_impact: May support new dispatchable generation investment. Credits expected to provide $1-2B/year in additional generator revenue.
quantitative_impact: Expected to support 3-7 GW of new dispatchable capacity

name: Clean Power Plan
description: Obama-era regulation setting first-ever carbon emission limits for existing power plants. Would have required 32% reduction from 2005 levels by 2030.
market_impact: Stayed by Supreme Court before implementation. Created planning uncertainty. Many utilities proceeded with coal retirements anyway due to economics.
quantitative_impact: Never implemented; repealed 2019
